items.title: Allen–Cahn and Cahn–Hilliard double-well gradient flows
items.statement: Allen–Cahn and Cahn–Hilliard gradient flows with quartic double-well energy, no-flux boundary conditions, finite-energy initial data, and explicit dimension caveats.

references.title: Jie Shen and Xiaofeng Yang, Numerical approximations of Allen-Cahn and Cahn-Hilliard equations, Discrete and Continuous Dynamical Systems A 28 (2010), 1669–1691
references.locator: §1, equations (1.1)–(1.5), PDF pp. 1–2: the two no-flux models, their common energy, and their L2 and H−1 gradient-flow identities.

references.title: Jie Shen, Jie Xu, and Jiang Yang, The scalar auxiliary variable (SAV) approach for gradient flows, Journal of Computational Physics 353 (2018), 407–416
references.locator: §1, equations (1.1)–(1.3), PDF pp. 1–2: the H−1 Cahn–Hilliard gradient flow and energy dissipation identity.

items.axiom_base: The core definitions do not use a choice axiom. Assume the Axiom of Choice only when invoking the cited d=2 or d=3 Sobolev embedding consequences, whose suppliers declare that hypothesis.

items.title: No-flux finite-volume and conforming realizations for phase fields
items.statement: Connected no-flux TPFA graph realization and a conforming interval P1 realization with exact mass and potential energy.

references.title: R. Eymard, T. Gallouët, and R. Herbin, Finite Volume Methods, Handbook of Numerical Analysis, Vol. VII, 2000; complete updated author text
references.locator: Chapter 9 §9.2, Definition 9.1 and equations (9.17)–(9.23), printed pp. 35–42, for orthogonal cell-centred transmissibilities and conservative face fluxes; Chapter 10 §§10.1–10.2, printed pp. 63–68, for the pure-diffusion Neumann scheme, mean-zero gauge, and connected-cell kernel.

references.title: Jérôme Droniou, Finite volume schemes for diffusion equations: introduction to and review of modern methods, 2014
references.locator: §2, equations (2.1)–(2.7), PDF pp. 8–10, for orthogonality, the two-point flux, the discrete energy, and the fact that the Dirichlet boundary term belongs only to the Dirichlet branch.

references.title: Jie Shen and Xiaofeng Yang, Numerical approximations of Allen-Cahn and Cahn-Hilliard equations, Discrete and Continuous Dynamical Systems A 28 (2010), 1669–1691
references.locator: §3.1, mixed Cahn–Hilliard formulation (3.1), printed p. 1681 / PDF p. 12: the two second-order weak equations and homogeneous Neumann conventions.

items.title: Kernel, range, and mean-zero inverse for the no-flux Laplacian
items.statement: Self-adjointness, nonnegativity, constant kernel, mean-zero range and inverse, and a fixed-mesh Poincare bound for both connected no-flux realizations.
items.strategy: Use the symmetric energy form and connectedness to identify the kernel; use rank-nullity for the range and inverse; minimize the positive Rayleigh quotient on the mean-zero sphere for the mesh-dependent bound.
items.axiom_base: No choice axiom is used; all spaces are finite-dimensional.

references.title: R. Eymard, T. Gallouët, and R. Herbin, Finite Volume Methods, Handbook of Numerical Analysis, Vol. VII, 2000; complete updated author text
references.locator: Chapter 10, §§10.1–10.2, printed pp. 63–68: the Neumann finite-volume scheme, compatibility, constant kernel, and mean-zero gauge.

references.title: Jérôme Droniou, Finite volume schemes for diffusion equations: introduction to and review of modern methods, 2014
references.locator: §2.1, equations (2.6)–(2.7), PDF pp. 9–10, for the symmetric graph energy and the distinction between interior and boundary terms.

items.title: Uniform interval stability of the phase-field L2 projector
items.statement: Uniform H1 stability, L2 approximation, strong H1 convergence for every H1 input, and strong L2 convergence for every L2 input of the interval L2 projector.
items.strategy: Derive interpolation error and an inverse estimate, combine them with L2 contraction for uniform H1 stability, prove smooth H1 approximation, and extend by density to every H1 function.
items.axiom_base: Assume the Axiom of Choice through the supplier providing the unique absolutely-continuous representative of each one-dimensional H1 class, so nodal interpolation is well-defined; its Countable Choice consequence also supplies smooth L2 approximants for the density argument.

references.title: Christian Clason, Introduction to Finite Element Methods, complete lecture notes, arXiv:1709.08618v2
references.locator: Chapter 12 §§12.1–12.2, PDF pp. 102–105: conforming spatial subspaces, the L2 projector, and projector stability hypotheses in parabolic discretization.

references.title: R. Eymard, T. Gallouët, and R. Herbin, Finite Volume Methods, Handbook of Numerical Analysis, Vol. VII, 2000; complete updated author text
references.locator: Chapter 9 §9.2, printed pp. 35–42: the one-dimensional orthogonal dual mesh and its center-to-center transmissibilities.

items.title: Stabilized semi-implicit phase-field step
items.statement: Alternative stabilized semi-implicit AC and CH updates with no stability, physical energy, maximum-principle, or error claim.

references.title: Jie Shen and Xiaofeng Yang, Numerical approximations of Allen-Cahn and Cahn-Hilliard equations, Discrete and Continuous Dynamical Systems A 28 (2010), 1669–1691
references.locator: §2.1.1, equation (2.6), PDF pp. 3–4, for stabilized Allen–Cahn; §3.1.1, equation (3.7), PDF pp. 12–13, for stabilized Cahn–Hilliard. Their stability statements require the hypotheses stated there and are not imported here.

items.title: First-order scalar-auxiliary-variable Cahn–Hilliard step
items.statement: First-order Cahn–Hilliard SAV linear system with an independently evolving auxiliary scalar.

references.title: Jie Shen, Jie Xu, and Jiang Yang, The scalar auxiliary variable (SAV) approach for gradient flows, Journal of Computational Physics 353 (2018), 407–416
references.locator: §3, equations (3.1)–(3.2), PDF pp. 5–6, for the SAV reformulation and modified energy; §4, equations (4.2)–(4.5), PDF pp. 8–10, for the Cahn–Hilliard SAV system and its discrete energy law.

items.title: Backward-Euler convex splitting for Allen–Cahn and Cahn–Hilliard
items.statement: Finite-dimensional backward-Euler convex-splitting minimization steps for AC and CH.

references.title: Jie Shen, Jie Xu, and Jiang Yang, The scalar auxiliary variable (SAV) approach for gradient flows, Journal of Computational Physics 353 (2018), 407–416
references.locator: §2.1, equations (2.1)–(2.2), PDF pp. 2–3: the first-order convex-splitting recurrence and its discrete energy inequality.

items.title: The SAV step is uniquely solvable and dissipates a modified energy
items.statement: Unique solvability and exact modified-energy dissipation identity for the backward-Euler SAV CH step.
items.strategy: Show the homogeneous linear SAV system has trivial kernel, then pair the three update equations to derive conservation and the exact modified-energy identity.

references.title: Jie Shen, Jie Xu, and Jiang Yang, The scalar auxiliary variable (SAV) approach for gradient flows, Journal of Computational Physics 353 (2018), 407–416
references.locator: §3, equation (3.2) and Theorem 3.1, PDF pp. 5–6, for SAV modified-energy dissipation; §4, PDF pp. 8–10, for the Cahn–Hilliard specialization. The local proof below supplies the backward-Euler identity.

references.title: Jie Shen and Xiaofeng Yang, Numerical approximations of Allen-Cahn and Cahn-Hilliard equations, Discrete and Continuous Dynamical Systems A 28 (2010), 1669–1691
references.locator: §3.1, equation (3.1), PDF pp. 12–13: mixed no-flux Cahn–Hilliard formulation and the gradient-energy pairing.

items.title: Existence, uniqueness, mass conservation, and energy decay of a convex-splitting step
items.statement: Unique finite-dimensional convex-splitting minimizers, Euler equations, CH mass conservation, and physical discrete-energy decay.
items.strategy: Establish quartic coercivity and convexity, minimize on the full or fixed-mean finite-dimensional domain, derive Euler equations, and apply convexity plus the update identity to obtain energy decay.
items.axiom_base: No choice axiom is used; minimizers are attained in finite-dimensional spaces by coercivity and finite-dimensional compactness.

references.title: Jie Shen, Jie Xu, and Jiang Yang, The scalar auxiliary variable (SAV) approach for gradient flows, Journal of Computational Physics 353 (2018), 407–416
references.locator: §2.1, equations (2.1)–(2.2), PDF pp. 2–3: the convex-splitting energy inequality and minimization interpretation. The proof below supplies the full argument for the selected discrete realizations.

references.title: Jing Guo, Cheng Wang, Steven M. Wise, and Xingye Yue, An H2 convergence of a second-order convex-splitting finite difference scheme for the three-dimensional Cahn–Hilliard equation, Communications in Mathematical Sciences 14 (2016), 489–515
references.locator: §1, equation (1.4), PDF pp. 489–490, for the first-order Cahn–Hilliard convex-splitting recurrence; §2.2, Theorems 2.2–2.3, PDF pp. 493–494, for the related strict-convexity and modified-energy route.

references.title: R. Eymard, T. Gallouët, and R. Herbin, Finite Volume Methods, Handbook of Numerical Analysis, Vol. VII, 2000; complete updated author text
references.locator: Chapter 10 §§10.1–10.2, printed pp. 63–68, for the Neumann finite-volume mean-zero compatibility and constant-kernel argument.

items.title: First-order time error under smooth fixed-mesh solutions
items.statement: First-order fixed-mesh temporal error in L2 for AC and H-1 for CH under smooth semidiscrete trajectories.
items.strategy: Bound the backward-Euler residual and use monotonicity and discrete Gronwall in L2 for AC and the mean-zero H-1 inner product for CH.

references.title: Jie Shen and Xiaofeng Yang, Numerical approximations of Allen-Cahn and Cahn-Hilliard equations, Discrete and Continuous Dynamical Systems A 28 (2010), 1669–1691
references.locator: §§2.1–2.2 and 3.1–3.2, printed pp. 1672–1688 / PDF pp. 3–19: stability arguments and error estimates under explicit smoothness, truncation, and epsilon-dependent constants. The local theorem below proves the selected backward-Euler split in a fixed finite-dimensional space.

references.title: Jie Shen, Jie Xu, and Jiang Yang, The scalar auxiliary variable (SAV) approach for gradient flows, Journal of Computational Physics 353 (2018), 407–416
references.locator: §2.1, equations (2.1)–(2.2), PDF pp. 2–3: first-order convex splitting, used only as a comparison of the same implicit/explicit split.

items.title: One-dimensional mesh and time convergence of convex-splitting phase flows
items.statement: One-dimensional subsequential mesh/time convergence to the no-flux weak AC and CH equations at fixed epsilon.
items.strategy: Derive uniform energy, chemical-potential, and time-derivative bounds; apply discrete Aubin–Lions and weak compactness; pass projected tests and the quartic nonlinearities to the limit.
items.axiom_base: Assume the Axiom of Choice. It is used by the PE12 discrete Aubin–Lions compactness theorem and by the weak subsequence extraction in the separable Bochner Hilbert supplier; the finite-dimensional step theorem is choice-free.

references.title: Jie Shen and Xiaofeng Yang, Numerical approximations of Allen-Cahn and Cahn-Hilliard equations, Discrete and Continuous Dynamical Systems A 28 (2010), 1669–1691
references.locator: §§2.2 and 3.2, printed pp. 1676–1688 / PDF pp. 7–19: conditional smooth-solution error bounds, explicit epsilon dependence, and the role of spatial approximation.

references.title: Jing Guo, Cheng Wang, Steven M. Wise, and Xingye Yue, An H2 convergence of a second-order convex-splitting finite difference scheme for the three-dimensional Cahn–Hilliard equation, Communications in Mathematical Sciences 14 (2016), 489–515
references.locator: §4, Theorem 4.1 and proof, PDF pp. 22–25 / printed pp. 503–507: convergence only under explicit periodicity, smoothness, and time-step restrictions for that distinct second-order scheme.

references.title: Christian Clason, Introduction to Finite Element Methods, complete lecture notes, arXiv:1709.08618v2
references.locator: Chapter 12 §§12.1–12.2, PDF pp. 102–105: conforming spatial subspaces, time-discrete compactness, and the assumptions used in a parabolic finite-element limit.

references.title: R. Eymard, T. Gallouët, and R. Herbin, Finite Volume Methods, Handbook of Numerical Analysis, Vol. VII, 2000; complete updated author text
references.locator: Chapter 9 §9.2, equations (9.17)–(9.23), printed pp. 40–42: the center-to-center two-point stiffness on the one-dimensional orthogonal dual grid.

title: Phase-field and dissipative gradient-flow computation — Examples

items.title: The one-dimensional Allen–Cahn double-well front
items.statement: Exact finite-energy tanh heteroclinic solving the one-dimensional stationary AC Euler–Lagrange equation on R.
items.strategy: Differentiate the tanh profile, verify the ODE exactly, and integrate its exponentially decaying energy density.

references.title: Jie Shen and Xiaofeng Yang, Numerical approximations of Allen-Cahn and Cahn-Hilliard equations, Discrete and Continuous Dynamical Systems A 28 (2010), 1669–1691
references.locator: §1, equations (1.1)–(1.5), PDF pp. 1–2: the Allen–Cahn Euler–Lagrange equation and double-well model. The heteroclinic profile is verified directly here.

items.title: Interface width and a grid that misses the transition
items.statement: Exact quartic-front transition width and a shifted grid with no samples in that transition.
items.strategy: Invert the monotone tanh profile at levels ±1/2 and place a uniform grid halfway between sample points.

references.title: Jie Shen and Xiaofeng Yang, Numerical approximations of Allen-Cahn and Cahn-Hilliard equations, Discrete and Continuous Dynamical Systems A 28 (2010), 1669–1691
references.locator: §1, printed pp. 1669–1671 / PDF pp. 1–2: the parameter ε represents the interfacial width; the exact profile and sampling calculation are derived here.

items.title: Modified-energy decay alone does not imply physical-energy decay
items.statement: Scalar pairs showing that a decrease in modified energy alone does not logically imply physical-energy decrease.
items.strategy: Evaluate both energies on explicitly specified one-cell scalar pairs and compare the signs of their changes.

references.title: Jie Shen, Jie Xu, and Jiang Yang, The scalar auxiliary variable (SAV) approach for gradient flows, Journal of Computational Physics 353 (2018), 407–416
references.locator: §3, equation (3.2) and Remark 3.2(iv), PDF pp. 5–6: SAV dissipates a modified energy, while convergence of that modified energy to the exact physical energy needs additional assumptions.

items.title: A two-cell Cahn–Hilliard mass and energy ledger
items.statement: Exact two-cell no-flux CH step, unique cubic state, conserved mass, and strictly decreasing physical energy.
items.strategy: Reduce the mean-zero two-cell update to one scalar cubic, locate its unique root, and compute both discrete energies exactly.

references.title: R. Eymard, T. Gallouët, and R. Herbin, Finite Volume Methods, Handbook of Numerical Analysis, Vol. VII, 2000; complete updated author text
references.locator: Chapter 10 §§10.1–10.2, printed pp. 63–68, for the Neumann cell graph, conserved mean, and the mean-zero gauge; the two-cell ledger is computed exactly here.

references.title: Jing Guo, Cheng Wang, Steven M. Wise, and Xingye Yue, An H2 convergence of a second-order convex-splitting finite difference scheme for the three-dimensional Cahn–Hilliard equation, Communications in Mathematical Sciences 14 (2016), 489–515
references.locator: §1, equation (1.4), PDF pp. 1–2 / printed pp. 489–490: the standard first-order convex-splitting Cahn–Hilliard update.
